Can you check your driver settings and ensure that there are is no contrast boosting / sharpening setting? I had a similar issue a few years ago (but with an AMD graphics card) and the problem turned out to be that AMD had quietly enabled contrast boost in all games and the Godot editor was accidentally included. 

I think this would be the setting to turn off https://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/4920/~/how-to-enable-image-sharpening-in-the-nvidia-control-panel

Hi I wanted to add that this recent update from Nvidia broke the Transparent BG option for the SubViewport node for me.

This issue has been confirmed many times already, and it's a problem with the latest Nvidia 572.16+ drivers. A lot of Vulkan applications seem to be affected, and Nvidia is aware of the problem.

There's nothing we can do on the Godot side to mitigate this, so affected users can either:

- Roll back the driver to a previous version
- Wait for Nvidia to update their drivers with a fix
- Configure Godot to use Direct3D 12 instead of Vulkan (set `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows` to `d3d12`)
- Refer to the official Nvidia feedback thread for updates: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/forums/game-ready-drivers/13/556258/geforce-grd-57216-feedback-thread-released-13025/

**Please do not add comments to this issue only to confirm that you're also affected, the issue is already known.** Instead, you can upvote the original post to indicate that you're also affected.

Hello there i found a fix: Nvidia Control Panel > Manage 3D Settings > Vulkan/OpenGL present method > set to Prefer native



![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ecc2c4b-bac9-4bc3-8224-625aafee352d)

> Hello there i found a fix: Nvidia Control Panel > Manage 3D Settings > Vulkan/OpenGL present method > set to Prefer native

This is more of a workaround than a fix. The DXGI swapchain is needed for features like fullscreen game capture and windowed direct scanout. So you might lose the ability to take screenshots or use G-SYNC or HDR in some cases.

Instead of changing the setting globally, you might want to change it on a per-app basis under the Program Settings tab. Either way, just remember to put the setting back on Auto once nVidia fixes this on their end.
